chunks: And a group informed us, from Abu Muhammad Harun, from Muhammad ibn Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, who said:

We performed Hajj in some years after the demise of Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him). I entered upon Ahmad ibn Ishaq in the City of Peace (Baghdad) and saw Abu Amr with him. I said: 'This Shaykh,' pointing to Ahmad ibn Ishaq, 'and he is a trustworthy and admirable man before us, has narrated to us about you such and such.' I narrated to him what had preceded, meaning what we had mentioned regarding the virtue and status of Abu Amr. I said: 'You are now among those who do not doubt in his word and truthfulness, so I ask you by the right of Allah and by the right of the two Imams who declared you trustworthy, have you seen the son of Abu Muhammad, who is the Master of the Age (peace be upon him)?' He wept, then said: 'On condition that you do not inform anyone with this as long as I am alive.' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'I have indeed seen him (peace be upon him), and his neck is like this'—meaning it was the most beautiful and complete of necks. I said: 'And the name?' He said: 'You have been forbidden from that.'

key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ: Ahmad ibn Ishaq (a key companion and narrator)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الزَّمَانِ: Master of the Age (referring to the 12th Imam)

ai.seo_question: Who confirmed the sighting of the Imam of the Age during the Minor Occultation?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the transition from the Minor Occultation to the Major Occultation, where Ahmad ibn Ishaq, a key figure among the Four Deputies, confirms the physical presence of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) while maintaining the secrecy of his name. The detail of his 'thick neck' serves as a specific physical identifier for the faithful during the period of widespread doubt, reinforcing the scholarly emphasis on the Imam's tangible yet hidden existence.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 316 - A group of scholars narrated to us from Abu Muhammad Harun from Muhammad Ibn Himam from Abdullah Ibn Ja’far that:

In a certain year, after the demise of Imam Hasan Askari (a.s), we performed Hajj. I went to Ahmad Ibn Ishaq at Baghdad and saw Abu Amr with him. I said: “This Shaykh,” pointing to Ahmad Ibn Ishaq, “and he is a trustworthy and admirable man before us, has narrated to us,” such and such. I narrated to him all of the narrative, which we mentioned above on the account of the eminent position of Abu Amr. I said: “You are now someone whose word and truthfulness is not dubitable. I beseech you for the sake of Allah and the sake of the two Imams who have declared you trustworthy, have you seen the son of Abu Muhammad, who is the Master of the Age?” He wept and then said: “You cannot inform anyone with this regard as long as I am alive.” I said: “Sure so.” He said: “I have verily seen him and his neck is like this.” He wanted to say that he has the most beautiful and wholesome of the necks. I asked, “And the name?” He said: “You have been forbidden from that.”
